finding.claim: The /admin/users/<uid>/ban handler does not enforce admin authorization. require_admin's 403 abort is swallowed by a broad except Exception, so any caller whose g.user is set (non-admin included) reaches do_ban(uid).
finding.source: Request path parameter <uid> (admin.py:15) and the caller identity in g.user (admin.py:17), which is set by upstream code not present in this repo. Any authenticated non-admin user can send the request.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 (state-changing user ban; stub here, real effect in the backend).

trace.note: user.get('is_admin') is falsy for a non-admin
abort(403) raises werkzeug HTTPException (subclass of Exception)
except Exception catches the 403 and does not re-raise
log.warning records the failed check and execution continues
returns {ok: true} to the non-admin caller

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is require_admin at line 17, which is neutralised by the except at line 18. No before_request hook, decorator, or role check exists in this file. Contrast unban at lines 24-28, which calls require_admin without a try and so correctly aborts. If g.user is unset, line 19 raises AttributeError outside the try and returns 500 before do_ban; that is a partial guard, not an authorization control, and it does not apply when upstream provides an empty or anonymous user dict. Upstream auth that sets g.user could not be inspected.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin at admin.py:17 (defined at admin.py:9-11). Its abort(403) is neutralised by the bare-ish `except Exception` at admin.py:18, which does not re-raise, so do_ban at admin.py:20 runs. No before_request hook, decorator, or role check exists in this file. If g.user is unset, admin.py:19 raises AttributeError outside the try and the request fails with 500 before do_ban, but that is not an authorization control and does not apply to an authenticated non-admin user whose g.user is a dict.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches admin.py (route at :14, require_admin at :17, check at :10, abort(403) at :11, swallowing except at :18, unconditional do_ban at :20); werkzeug's HTTPException subclasses Exception, so the 403 is caught and an authenticated non-admin with a dict-valued g.user reaches do_ban, while the unban handler at admin.py:26 shows the intended pattern.
